front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose of This Manual

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** (the "Agency") operates its community residence(s) for individuals with developmental disabilities in New Jersey. This includes group homes, supervised apartments and supportive living arrangements licensed by the NJ Department of Human Services (DHS) Office of Licensing under **N.J.A.C. 10:44A**. The Agency's services are approved and paid through the Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) as Individual Supports under the Community Care Program / Supports Program (NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration, Section 1115), fee-for-service.

The manual does four things:

1. **Meets the licensing requirement.** N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a) requires the licensee to develop and implement a written procedure manual and review its procedures annually. Under N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i), the manual goes to the Office of Licensing before the residence opens.
2. **Gives staff one reference for daily practice.** Each procedure has a unique title, a purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities, and reporting and recording requirements (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)).
3. **Reflects the rights and values the rules require.** Every procedure is designed around normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)). Individuals have the same rights as other citizens, and exercising those rights is never a cause for retribution (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-3.1).
4. **Supports accountability.** The manual helps the Agency show inspectors, DDD, Medicaid and the people it serves that it follows the rules.

## Scope

This manual covers **provider-managed community residences (group homes of up to 16 individuals) and supervised apartments (up to 4 individuals per apartment)**, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3 and described in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.1. It does **not** cover:

- Owner-occupied Community Care Residences (Family Care / Skill Development in a private home), which are licensed under **N.J.A.C. 10:44B**.
- Head-injury residences, which fall under **N.J.A.C. 10:44C**.

As described in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.1, licensing is voluntary where no resident needs personal guidance, as decided by the planning team.

## Important Notice: Customize, Adopt, Maintain and Train

This manual is a **template**. It is not legal advice and does not replace the regulations.

- **Customize it.** Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and other bracketed text with the Agency's actual information. Tailor each procedure to the Agency's program description, residences, staffing and the individuals it serves. A generic manual does not satisfy N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2.
- **Adopt it.** The Agency's governing body or governing authority must formally adopt the manual (record the adoption date and the approving signature in the adoption log) before it is used or submitted to the Office of Licensing.
- **Keep it current.** Review every procedure at least annually (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)). Also revise it whenever a rule, DDD policy, rate or program practice changes. N.J.A.C. 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026, and DHS has said further rulemaking may be necessary (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)). Keep a revision log.
- **Train staff on it.** Staff must be trained on the manual. N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7 requires training in all relevant policies not covered in orientation, delivered by a qualified trainer. Keep dated trainer and trainee signatures in the training records.
front_matter.how_to_use:
# How to Use This Manual

## Who should use it

- **Governing body / governing authority:** adopts the manual, approves revisions and oversees compliance.
- **Executive director / community agency head:** keeps the manual current, ensures it is implemented, and makes it available to the Office of Licensing and DDD.
- **Residence supervisors:** keep a working copy at each residence and use it to supervise and coach staff.
- **Direct support professionals (DSPs) and other staff:** read the procedures that apply to their duties, complete the training, and follow the steps as written.
- **Individuals, families, guardians and advocates:** the Agency's purposes and a description of its services must be made available to them and to the general public (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.1(a)). Decide which parts of the manual to share beyond that, as long as confidentiality requirements are met.

## Structure of each procedure

Each procedure follows the format required by N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a):

1. Unique title
2. Purpose
3. Sequential steps
4. Staff responsibilities
5. Reporting and recording requirements

When customizing, confirm each procedure meets normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning.

## Required contents checklist (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b))

The manual must include, at a minimum, the items below. Use this list to confirm nothing is missing before submission.

| # | Required content | Notes from the rule |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Philosophy | |
| 2 | Table of organization | |
| 3 | Central Registry compliance | |
| 4 | New Employee Orientation Checklist | |
| 5 | Major emergency / evacuation plan | Includes indoor air below 68°F or above 82°F for four consecutive hours |
| 6 | Medical emergencies | 9-1-1 call for life-threatening emergencies (Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:42A) |
| 7 | Emergency coverage / on-call | |
| 8 | Unusual incident reporting | Written prohibition on abuse, neglect and exploitation, and the obligation to report each allegation |
| 9 | Investigations | |
| 10 | Fiscal management of personal funds | See also N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.10 |
| 11 | Safekeeping of valuables | |
| 12 | List and schedule of charges and fees | |
| 13 | Complaint / grievance procedure | At least two levels; the last involves the licensee or executive director |
| 14 | Separate internal communication / critical-information log | |
| 15 | Admissions | Per N.J.A.C. 10:44A-4 |
| 16 | Confidentiality | Per N.J.A.C. 10:41-2 |
| 17 | Medication administration and self-medication | See also N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7(b) and 5.2 |
| 18 | Controlled dangerous substance testing of employees | N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 |
| 19 | Exchange of contact information with involved family / guardians | N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6 |
| 20 | Child Abuse Registry check | |
| 21 | Video / audio monitoring of common areas | If applicable |
| 22 | Continuous quality improvement system | |

The Agency's own procedures should also cover the related areas below. Check each one against the current rule text.

- Personnel and employee screening, including TB screening (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.4)
- Minimum staff qualifications (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5)
- Staff training (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7)
- Staff coverage and schedules (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.8)
- Individual records (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.9)
- Rights and the Human Rights Committee (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-3.1)
- Individual Habilitation Plans (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-4.3)
- Health and safety (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-5.1 to 5.8)
- Fire safety and physical environment (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-6.1 to 6.17)

## Steps to put the manual into operation

1. **Customize.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholders. Add the Agency's program description, table of organization, fee schedule, contact lists and forms.
2. **Verify against current rules.** Confirm each cited section, subsection letter and numeric requirement against the current text of N.J.A.C. 10:44A. Several items in this manual are flagged for confirmation (see *Items to confirm* in the Regulatory Framework section).
3. **Obtain legal / compliance review.** Counsel should review the manual, especially the enforcement provisions of P.L.2025, c.280, whose text has not been reviewed for this manual.
4. **Adopt.** The governing body adopts the manual by formal action. Record the date and signatures.
5. **Submit.** Under N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i), the procedure manual goes to the Office of Licensing before opening, and job descriptions then go to DDD.
6. **Train.** Train all staff and document the training (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7(c), (e), (g)). Keep records in the administrative office with the curriculum or training plan and dated trainer and trainee signatures.
7. **Implement and monitor.** Keep a working copy at each residence. Use the continuous quality improvement system to check that procedures are followed in practice.
8. **Review and revise.** Review annually at a minimum, and sooner when rules, DDD policy or Agency practice changes. Re-adopt revised sections, re-train staff and update the revision log.

## Defined terms

This manual uses the terms defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3, including Abuse, Exploitation, Central Registry, Critical information, Direct support professional, Governing authority, Community agency head, Executive director, Behavior support plan, Falsification, Fiduciary capacity, Guardian, Authorization to operate, Eviction, and Service plan / planning team. Use these terms consistently.

## Inspection readiness

Office of Licensing inspections are annual and may be unannounced, and are expected to increase beginning in 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents. Partial compliance can result in a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Keep the manual, training records and supporting documentation organized and available at all times.

citations.title: Purpose and scope
citations.requirement: Chapter sets minimum requirements for residential services to people with DD. It applies to provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments. Community care residences (Family Care/Skill Development in a private home) are licensed under 10:44B. Head-injury residences fall under 10:44C. Licensing is voluntary where no resident needs personal guidance, as decided by the planning team.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Community residence: up to 16 individuals, not on the grounds of or immediately adjacent to public institutions serving a similar population. Supervised apartment: up to 4 individuals per apartment. Full license: up to one year. Also defines Abuse, Exploitation, Central Registry, Critical information, Direct support professional, Governing authority, Community agency head, Executive director, Behavior support plan, Falsification, Fiduciary capacity, Guardian, Authorization to operate (permits operation past license expiration when an inspection is delayed), Eviction, and Service plan/planning team.

citations.title: Application for licensure
citations.requirement: (a) Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider plus the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. (b) No agency head may be paid or contracted until criminal history clearance under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69; owner/licensee also checked if different from the agency head. (c)(1) Application contents include a table of organization, CVs, owners, 24 months of service history with survey results and plans of correction, penalties/fines record, CPA examination for two fiscal years, and 3 professional references each. (d)(1) 45 days to complete or the application may be denied, with a 6-month bar on reapplying. (g) Written decision within 60 calendar days. (i) The procedure manual goes to the Office of Licensing before opening, then job descriptions go to DDD. (j) No operation without Office of Licensing authorization. (k) DHS inspection without limitation or notice. (l) Annual on-site inspection. (m) No license after denial by any State agency for substantial noncompliance. (n) No license if a final finding of discrimination exists.

citations.title: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee's purposes and a description of its services must be made available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the general public. Other subsections of 2.1 were not read.

citations.title: Development and maintenance of procedure manual
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee develops and implements a written procedure manual. Procedures are reviewed annually. Each procedure is designed on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning. Each has a unique title, purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities and reporting/recording requirements. (b) Required contents: 1 philosophy; 2 table of organization; 3 Central Registry compliance; 4 New Employee Orientation Checklist; 5 major emergency/evacuation plan, including indoor air below 68F or above 82F for four consecutive hours; 6 medical emergencies with a 9-1-1 call for life-threatening emergencies (Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:42A); 7 emergency coverage/on-call; 8 unusual incident reporting with a written prohibition on abuse, neglect and exploitation and the obligation to report each allegation; 9 investigations; 10 fiscal management of personal funds; 11 safekeeping of valuables; 12 list and schedule of charges and fees; 13 complaint/grievance procedure with at least two levels, the last involving the licensee or executive director; 14 separate internal communication/critical-information log; 15 admissions per 10:44A-4; 16 confidentiality per N.J.A.C. 10:41-2; 17 medication administration and self-medication; 18 controlled dangerous substance testing of employees (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5); 19 exchange of contact information with involved family/guardians (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6); 20 Child Abuse Registry check; 21 video/audio monitoring of common areas, if applicable; 22 continuous quality improvement system.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Personnel requirements, including employee screening. All employees who may contact individuals must comply with the screening requirements. A provider-hosted copy of the 2023 text shows a TB screen (Mantoux 5 TU PPD or IGRA blood test) within one year before or upon starting work, with written results submitted to the licensee. The 2005 text also required annual repeat testing, so confirm the current subsection letter and any repeat interval.

citations.title: Minimum staff qualifications
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee or executive director has a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive DD management experience (at least two supervisory at a senior/administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal/qualitative standards. (b) Residence supervisor has a high school diploma or equivalent plus one year of DD experience. (c) DSPs are 18 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent. (d) DSPs can communicate with the individuals they work with. (e) DSPs can provide the direct assistance or training required. (f) Licensee verifies professional credentials required by law for employed or contracted professionals.

citations.title: Staff training
citations.requirement: (a) Within 90 days of employment each DSP completes Division basic training: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, first aid and CPR from an ECC-compliant entity, each with a valid certificate on file. (b) Medication training and demonstrated competency come before administering any medication, and competency is shown annually. (c) Training in all relevant policies not covered in orientation. (d) Specialized training within 90 days of employment: feeding techniques (feeding tube duties delegated to nursing), mobility devices and transport, seizure/physical/medical needs, mental health needs, and behavior support plans. (e) Training records kept in the administrative office with a curriculum/training plan, dated trainer and trainee signatures, and Division-required results. (f) Additional training is allowed without Division approval. (g) Training under (c) is delivered by a qualified trainer.

citations.title: Staff coverage
citations.requirement: (a) A written staff schedule for at least two weeks is available at each residence with full staff names. It shows on-site coverage per the program description, and an in-charge employee for each shift. Temporary agency staff may not be designated in-charge unless all 2.7 training is complete and a written policy states the licensee assumes responsibility and liability. (b) Each required specialized training is completed by at least one person on each shift. (c) Staff need not be on site when no individuals are present, but trained, paid agency staff familiar with the individuals must be available for emergencies. (d) Group home/supervised apartment staff are on site whenever any individual is present, per supervision needs. (e) The staff residence/office of a supervised apartment program is located so response time fits supervision needs. No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A.

citations.title: Records of individuals receiving services
citations.requirement: (a) An individual file is kept for each individual receiving services. (b) Files for group home and supervised apartment residents are kept at the residence. Contents include full name, DOB and sex; Social Security and Medicaid/insurance numbers; and dates of admission, readmission, transfer or discharge. The remaining required contents and any retention period were not read.

citations.title: Individual financial records: personal funds
citations.requirement: The licensee keeps a written record of all financial arrangements and transactions involving individuals' entrusted funds. Each individual and guardian has access to it on request, and copies are provided on request. The 2005 text also required the licensee to manage funds so as not to jeopardize benefit entitlements. Confirm the current subsection.

citations.title: Advocacy and rights: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Services recognize that people with disabilities have the same rights as other citizens, and exercising rights is never a cause for retribution. (b) Licensee complies with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. (c) Staff are familiar with and observe the rights listed in the Division's rights document. The licensee provides the rights document and gets acknowledgments on admission. (d) Individuals receive training and support to understand options, make choices and exercise rights. Rights are not limited because an individual has a guardian or family. (e) The licensee uses a Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A. House rules involve the affected individuals, are necessary for order, and do not infringe on others' rights.

citations.title: Individual Habilitation Plan (IHP)
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee has and implements a procedure for developing, implementing, reviewing and evaluating each individual's habilitation or service plan under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-10 et seq. (b) The plan and monthly documentation of progress are kept in the individual's record. (c) The comprehensive IHP includes 14 elements: cover page; evaluation summaries; progress on prior goals; preferences, capabilities and needs; goals; measurable sequential objectives; method for each objective; team members and responsible persons; services with start dates, duration and frequency; barriers; guardianship review; meeting summary/addendum (disagreement may be noted); attendance sign-off; and authorization for approved individual expenses.

citations.title: Subchapter 5 - Health and Safety
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 10:44A-5.1 to 5.8 per the LII table of contents. A DHS 2/14/2023 webinar says 5.1(g)8-9 added a CPR mask and protective gloves to first aid kit requirements. The 2005 text had 5.1 General health care and 5.3 Over-the-counter medications. The rest of the subchapter text was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement (health care, OTC medications, food/diets, restraint/behavioral supports, incident rules) before citing it individually.

citations.title: Prescription medication
citations.requirement: (a) Individuals self-administer to the extent possible, as determined by the planning team, documented in the record and following licensee procedure. (b) If the individual cannot, the licensee or designee assists and supervises administration as prescribed. (c) A record is kept of all medication administered, including individual's name, date and medication name. For PRN medication the label must show name, date, medication, dosage, interval, maximum amount per 24 hours, stop date where appropriate, and conditions for giving it. An Advanced Practice Nurse may prescribe (2023 amendment).

citations.title: Subchapter 6 - Fire Safety and Physical Environment
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 6.1 to 6.17 per the LII table of contents. Rule text seen indicates the licensee must obtain documentation of any required Fire Official inspection and registration with the Department of Community Affairs, and a certificate from the local enforcing authority (or documentation that none is issued). The individual section text, including drill frequency, was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement before citing it individually.

citations.title: Manual of Standards for Community Care Residences (scope exclusion)
citations.requirement: Owner-occupied Family Care/Skill Development living arrangements are licensed under 10:44B and not 10:44A. This manual covers provider-managed homes and apartments only.

citations.title: Notice of Readoption, N.J.A.C. 10:44A
citations.requirement: 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (new expiration February 17, 2033). DHS stated further rulemaking may be necessary. The section text cited here is the 2023-amended text, so recheck against the current rule each year.

citations.title: Enhanced Human Services enforcement authority over developmental disability providers (Jan 2026)
citations.requirement: Expands DHS enforcement authority over DD providers. The statute text was not reviewed, so counsel should read the penalty provisions.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care/home health services. NJ applies it to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through HHAeXchange. A Live-In Worker Attestation allows exclusion where the worker lives with the person served.

citations.cite: NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115); HCBS Statewide Transition Plan Addendum #3
citations.title: Authority for DDD Supports Program / Community Care Program
citations.requirement: DDD services are authorized under the 1115 demonstration (no longer 1915(c) since Nov 2017). NJ's HCBS settings transition plan applies to 10:44A homes.

citations.cite: DDD - Apply to Become a Provider
citations.title: Combined Application / Individual Supports provider approval
citations.requirement: Agencies that want to run a licensed residential setting submit the Combined Application and select Individual Supports. At least 24 months of documented direct-care service history is required, including survey/audit results and plans of correction.

citations.title: Annual audit and Fiscal Sustainability Report
citations.requirement: An annual financial statement audit is required for agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement. The audit follows GAAS. The Fiscal Sustainability Report is due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30).

citations.cite: DDD Division Update, January 22, 2026; iRecord Rate Change (1/1/2026)
citations.title: DSP/DSP Supervisor wage pass-through
citations.requirement: Rates for nine agency-provided services rose 1/1/2026. Agencies must pass through about $0.46/hr as a base-wage increase to DSPs and DSP Supervisors no later than 3/1/2026, with retroactive pay. It cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.

citations.cite: NJ DHS Office of Licensing (OPIA) provider page
citations.title: Inspections, provisional licenses and enforcement posture
citations.requirement: Annual and unannounced inspections, which increase beginning 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents. Partial compliance can produce a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Housing must be cleared with DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquisition.

citations.cite: DDD FFS FAQ: Becoming a Medicaid Provider
citations.title: Medicaid approval before billing
citations.requirement: An agency must be Medicaid-approved to submit claims for DDD services, and the same Combined Application is used for Medicaid and DDD approval. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without a Medicaid ID.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Licensee/Executive Director and Residence Supervisor Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, licensee, executive director/community agency head, residence supervisors and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To establish who is accountable for the operation of [AGENCY NAME]'s community residences and supervised apartments, to set the minimum qualifications for those in leadership roles, and to make our purposes and services known to individuals, families, guardians, advocates and the public, as N.J.A.C. 10:44A requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by a governing authority that appoints a licensee or executive director, who is responsible for day-to-day compliance with N.J.A.C. 10:44A and for the health, safety and rights of every individual served. Each residence has a residence supervisor with delegated duties. The licensee or executive director holds a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive management experience in developmental disabilities (at least two years in a supervisory role at a senior or administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal and qualitative standards. Each residence supervisor holds a high school diploma or equivalent and at least one year of experience in developmental disabilities. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written philosophy statement and a table of organization showing lines of authority in this manual. We verify the professional credentials of every employed or contracted professional the law requires to be credentialed. Our purposes and a description of our services are available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the public on request and without charge.

definitions.definition: The person or body (owner, board of trustees or equivalent) with ultimate legal responsibility for [AGENCY NAME] and its licensed programs.
The person or entity to whom the Office of Licensing issues the license to operate a community residence.
The person responsible for the overall administration of the agency and its programs, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.
The staff member responsible for the daily operation of a residence, including supervision of direct support professionals and implementation of individual plans.
A chart of agency positions, reporting relationships and lines of authority.
A staff member who provides direct assistance, training and support to individuals.

procedures: The governing authority adopts a written philosophy statement based on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning, and reviews it at least annually. The statement is filed at the front of this manual.
The governing authority appoints the licensee or executive director in writing and records the appointment in the governing authority's minutes.

Before appointment, the governing authority's designee confirms the candidate meets the education and experience requirements for the licensee or executive director. The designee obtains the degree verification, a CV and employment history showing the required years of progressive management experience, and at least two years in a senior supervisory role.
No licensee or executive director is paid or engaged until the criminal history clearance process described in GOV-02 and STF-02 is complete.

The executive director appoints each residence supervisor in writing. The HR designee verifies the diploma or equivalent and one year of developmental disabilities experience before the start date and files the proof in the personnel record (STF-05).

The executive director maintains the table of organization showing every position, who reports to whom, and who is in charge when the supervisor is absent. The executive director updates it within 14 calendar days of any change in a position and distributes the revision under GOV-03.

The executive director maintains a written job description for every position on the table of organization, including duties, qualifications and reporting line, and makes each job description available to DDD when requested.

The executive director delegates daily operations to residence supervisors in writing, but retains responsibility for compliance. The executive director reviews each residence at least monthly (on-site visit, record review and staff discussion) and documents the review.

The HR designee verifies the professional credential (license, certification or registration) of every nurse, therapist, behavior specialist or other credentialed professional, employed or contracted, before that person provides service. The designee checks the credential's expiration date and files a copy of the verification in the personnel or contractor file. The designee re-verifies before each expiration date.

The executive director reports at least quarterly to the governing authority on census, incidents, complaints, inspection results, staffing and quality improvement findings (GOV-04). The governing authority records its review and any directions in its minutes.

The executive director makes the agency's purposes and a description of its services available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the public. The summary is given at the first inquiry, is posted in each residence's common area, and is provided in accessible formats on request (IR-09).

The executive director reviews this policy annually with the governing authority, along with the table of organization and philosophy statement, and records the review date on the document-control log (GOV-03).

If the executive director or a residence supervisor position becomes vacant, the governing authority designates a qualified interim person within one business day. The designee must meet the qualifications of this policy. The change is documented and the table of organization is revised.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the philosophy, appoints the licensee/executive director, reviews quarterly reports and ensures resources to meet licensing standards.
Holds overall responsibility for licensing compliance, appoints and supervises residence supervisors, maintains the table of organization and ensures credentials are verified.
Runs the daily operation of the residence, supervises DSPs, implements individual plans and reports problems to the executive director.
Verifies qualifications and professional credentials, and keeps the verification records current.

documentation: Philosophy statement with annual review date
Table of organization with revision dates
Governing authority minutes showing appointments and quarterly reviews
Qualification verification for the executive director and each residence supervisor
Professional credential verification log
Job descriptions for all positions
Monthly executive director residence review notes
Written summary of purposes and services

policies.title: Licensure, Authorization to Operate and DDD/Medicaid Provider Approval
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, executive director, administrative staff and residence supervisors
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] operates each community residence and supervised apartment only with Office of Licensing authorization and active DDD/Medicaid provider approval, stays within licensed capacity and siting rules, and keeps its license in good standing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not own or operate a community residence or supervised apartment, accept an individual, or bill for services unless it holds Office of Licensing authorization and DDD/Medicaid approval for Individual Supports. This policy applies to provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44A. Family-care homes are licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44B and are outside this manual. No person is placed before approval is in hand. Each residence stays within licensed capacity: up to 16 individuals per community residence and up to 4 individuals per supervised apartment. No residence is located on the grounds of, or immediately adjacent to, a public institution serving a similar population. The full license is issued for up to one year. [AGENCY NAME] is open to inspection by the Department of Human Services at any time, without limitation or notice, and submits only truthful information to the State.

definitions.definition: A residence for up to 16 individuals with developmental disabilities, not on or immediately adjacent to the grounds of a public institution serving a similar population.
An apartment shared by up to 4 individuals with developmental disabilities, with supports from the licensee.
A license issued by the Office of Licensing for up to one year.
A license issued when compliance is partial; two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal.
Written permission from the Office of Licensing that allows operation past the license expiration date when the inspection is delayed.
The application to become a Medicaid/DDD approved provider, submitted with the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider.
Knowingly making a false entry or statement in a record or submission, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.

procedures: Before taking any step to buy, lease or alter a property, the executive director confirms the site is not on or immediately adjacent to the grounds of a public institution serving a similar population. The executive director also obtains clearance from DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquiring the housing. The clearance is filed in the licensing file.

The executive director confirms that [AGENCY NAME] has at least 24 months of documented direct-care service history, including survey or audit results and plans of correction, before starting a new application.

The executive director prepares the Combined Application and the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider, selecting Individual Supports. The application includes a table of organization, CVs, ownership information, the 24-month service history with survey results and plans of correction, the record of penalties or fines, the CPA examination for two fiscal years, and three professional references for each required person.

The executive director verifies every statement and document in the application for accuracy before signature. The governing authority's chair reviews the final application. No one may alter, backdate or omit required information, because falsification is cause for denial.

No agency head is paid or contracted, and the owner/licensee if a different person, until the criminal history clearance process required by N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69 is complete. The HR designee files the clearance results.

Within 45 days of the initial submission, the executive director completes any missing elements the State requests. The administrative designee calendars the date on receipt of the notice. If the application is not completed in time it may be denied, and [AGENCY NAME] cannot reapply for six months.

The administrative designee tracks the written decision, which is due within 60 calendar days of a complete application, and records the decision date. A denial triggers a review by the governing authority and a written decision on any appeal or corrective action.

After application approval and before opening, the executive director submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing and then job descriptions to DDD (GOV-03). No individual is admitted until written Office of Licensing authorization is received and the DDD/Medicaid approval is confirmed.
After approval, the administrative designee verifies that [AGENCY NAME] has an active Medicaid provider ID for Individual Supports and files a copy. Billing may not start until this is done (GOV-05).

The executive director posts the current license in each residence in a place visible to individuals and visitors, and keeps a copy in the licensing file. The administrative designee calendars the license expiration date and begins renewal preparation at least 90 days before.

Each residence supervisor keeps the actual census within licensed capacity. The supervisor never accepts an additional person, even temporarily, that would exceed capacity. The executive director checks the census against the license at the monthly residence review.

The executive director maintains the agency in a state of continuous inspection readiness (GOV-07). The agency expects annual on-site inspections and unannounced visits, which are increasing beginning in 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, the physical plant and insurance documents. Staff cooperate fully and give inspectors access to the premises and records without delay.

If the license expiration date is near and the Office of Licensing has not yet inspected, the executive director contacts the Office of Licensing in writing and requests a written authorization to operate. The authorization letter is kept on file. The agency does not rely on a verbal statement.

If the Office of Licensing issues a provisional license, the executive director convenes a leadership review within 5 business days, assigns owners and due dates to each deficiency (GOV-07), and reports weekly to the governing authority until the license returns to full status. [AGENCY NAME] treats a second consecutive provisional license as a risk of non-renewal.

The executive director confirms that [AGENCY NAME] has no prior denial by any State agency for substantial noncompliance and no final finding of discrimination, either of which would bar licensure. If any such finding arises, the executive director notifies the governing authority immediately and consults counsel.

N.J.A.C. 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026. The executive director checks the current text of the rule and any DDD or Office of Licensing notices at least annually, and whenever a notice is received, and updates this manual accordingly (GOV-03).

Prepares and certifies the application, ensures no operation or placement without authorization, maintains capacity limits and leads inspection readiness.
Tracks application deadlines, license and approval expiration dates, and keeps licensing and Medicaid records current.
Keeps census within licensed capacity, posts the license and cooperates with inspectors.

Criminal history clearance for agency head and owner/licensee

Authorization to operate letters

policies.title: Procedure Manual Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Executive director, residence supervisors, policy owners and all staff
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] develops, implements, reviews annually and controls a written procedure manual that meets N.J.A.C. 10:44A and is available to staff and inspectors.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains and implements a written procedure manual. Every procedure is designed on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning, and has a unique descriptive title, a purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities, and reporting and recording requirements. Procedures are reviewed at least annually and revised as necessary. A new applicant submits the manual to the Office of Licensing for approval after application approval and before opening. Job descriptions for each position on the table of organization are then submitted to DDD. Only the current version is in use, and staff are trained on every change.

definitions.definition: The written manual of policies and procedures required of the licensee by N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2.
The staff member assigned to maintain a specific policy and lead its annual review.
The record of each policy's version number, effective date, review date and distribution.

procedures: The executive director assigns each policy in the manual to a policy owner by title and records the assignment in the document control log.

Every policy uses the same format: unique title, purpose, policy, definitions, numbered sequential procedures, responsibilities, and documentation and reporting requirements. A policy that lacks any element is not issued.

Before issuing or revising a policy, the policy owner checks it against normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning, and writes a short note on the review form that this was done.

The manual is organized to include every topic N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b) requires: philosophy; table of organization; Central Registry compliance; new employee orientation checklist; emergency and evacuation plan; medical emergencies; emergency coverage and on-call; unusual incident reporting; investigations; fiscal management of personal funds; safekeeping of valuables; schedule of charges and fees; complaint and grievance procedure; critical-information log; admissions; confidentiality; medication administration; employee controlled dangerous substance testing; exchange of family and guardian contact information; Child Abuse Registry check; video and audio monitoring, if used; and continuous quality improvement. The executive director keeps a crosswalk of these items to the policy ID covering each one.

For a new application, the executive director submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing only after the application is approved and before opening. After that submission, the executive director sends job descriptions for each table-of-organization position to DDD.

The executive director opens the manual review each year in the same month. By the end of that month, each policy owner reviews their policies against the current rule text, DDD and Office of Licensing notices, incident and CQI data (GOV-04), and inspection findings. The owner records "no change" or the revisions on the review form.

Between annual reviews, the executive director triggers a review within 30 calendar days of any rule change, DDD or Office of Licensing notice, inspection deficiency, incident trend or CQI finding that affects a policy. The chapter was readopted effective February 17, 2026, and the executive director checks for further rulemaking at least annually.

The executive director approves every revision in writing. Each revised policy gets a new version number, an effective date and a summary of changes. The old version is stamped "superseded," dated, and archived for at least six years.

The administrative designee does not copy agency contact details, phone numbers or addresses for the Office of Licensing or DDD from older documents. Contact details are entered as current information and verified at each annual review.

Within 7 calendar days of an approved revision, the residence supervisor shares the change with all staff, records the training date and trainer, and obtains signed acknowledgment from each employee. New employees receive the current manual at orientation (STF-03).

A complete, current copy of the manual is kept in each residence and in the administrative office, and is available to staff on every shift, to individuals and guardians on request, and to inspectors on arrival.

When a revision changes how a service is delivered, the residence supervisor confirms that individual plans and daily routines are brought into line, and reports completion to the executive director within 30 calendar days.
The executive director reports the results of the annual manual review to the governing authority and records the date of the review in the minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the manual, approves all revisions, submits the manual and job descriptions for approval, and ensures annual review.
Review and revise assigned policies, and confirm design principles and rule currency.
Train staff on revisions, collect acknowledgments and keep the manual accessible.
Maintains the document control log, archive and rule-topic crosswalk.

documentation: Document control log with version, effective date and review date
Annual review forms for every policy
Crosswalk of required topics to policy IDs
Submission records to the Office of Licensing and DDD
Staff acknowledgment and training records

policies.title: Continuous Quality Improvement System and Incident/Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Executive director, residence supervisors, nursing and clinical staff, and all staff who report data
policies.purpose: To operate a written continuous quality improvement (CQI) system that uses data and the views of individuals and families to find patterns, correct problems and improve supports, and to review incidents and deaths so that lessons feed back into practice.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a CQI system with at least these elements: (1) a written plan for collecting and analyzing data to find patterns; (2) input from individuals, families and others; (3) a written summary of satisfaction surveys; (4) a written summary of outcomes assessments; and (5) an action plan based on the analysis. [AGENCY NAME] also reviews every reportable incident and every death internally. The review is not a replacement for the required report to the State or for any investigation (BSP-04, HW-05), and its findings are carried into the CQI action plan. If the Office of Licensing identifies a process or systemic problem and asks for an action plan and implementation results, we prepare and submit it promptly and verify the exact current requirement with the Office of Licensing.

definitions.definition: An ongoing, data-driven process to measure how well supports are delivered and to make improvements.
A structured review of whether individuals are reaching the goals and results in their plans.
A tool used to collect the views of individuals, families, guardians and others about services.
An internal review of each reportable incident to find causes and prevent recurrence.
An internal review of each death to identify care, communication or system issues that can improve practice. It is not a State-specified requirement and does not replace State reporting.
A written list of improvements, owners, due dates and measures of success.

procedures: The executive director appoints a CQI lead and a CQI team that includes at least a residence supervisor, the nurse, a DSP and, when willing, an individual served or a family member or guardian. The appointment is recorded in the CQI plan.

The CQI lead writes and maintains the data collection and analysis plan. For each data source it names what is collected, who collects it, how often and how it is analyzed. Data sources include incidents, medication errors, falls, hospital and emergency visits, grievances, rights restrictions, behavior data, missed or late services, staff turnover and vacancy, training completion, inspection findings and individual outcomes.
Each residence supervisor submits the monthly data to the CQI lead by the 10th of the following month. The CQI lead enters it into the tracking log and checks it for completeness.
The CQI team meets at least quarterly. It looks at the data by residence, shift, individual, time of day and type of event to find patterns, and records the findings in written minutes.

The CQI lead gathers input from individuals, families, guardians, advocates and staff at least annually, through surveys, interviews, individual plan meetings, house meetings or suggestion boxes. Individuals get help to give input in their preferred way (IR-09). Feedback is recorded without identifying anyone who wishes to remain anonymous.
The CQI lead issues a satisfaction survey at least annually and writes a summary of the results, including response rate, main themes and areas of concern.

The CQI lead prepares a written summary of outcomes assessments at least annually, using plan progress documentation (PCS-03) to show how many objectives were met, partly met or not met, and what changes were made.

For each reportable incident, the executive director or designee completes an internal incident review within 14 calendar days of the report. The review covers what happened, contributing factors, whether the response and reporting followed policy, whether the individual's plan needs change, and what prevents recurrence. Findings are added to the incident record and CQI log.

For each death, the executive director convenes an internal mortality review within 30 calendar days, with the nurse and residence supervisor and, as appropriate, other clinicians. The review looks at the individual's health history, recent changes, the emergency response, communication with clinicians and any agency-level lessons. It is conducted alongside, not instead of, State reports and investigations (HW-05, BSP-04).

Based on the analysis, the CQI team writes an action plan that names each problem, the improvement action, the responsible person, the due date and the measure of success. The executive director approves the action plan.
Every person assigned an action item reports progress at the next quarterly meeting. Items that miss their due date are escalated to the executive director with a revised date and reason.
The CQI lead re-measures the data after an action is implemented to see whether the pattern has improved, and records whether the action is closed, continued or revised.

If the Office of Licensing asks for an action plan or implementation results about a process or systemic problem, the executive director prepares the response within the deadline given, confirms what the Office of Licensing requires, and files the submission and its follow-up in the CQI record.
The executive director gives the governing authority a written CQI report at least quarterly and a summary annually, and shares survey and outcome summaries with individuals and families on request.
The CQI lead reviews this policy and the data collection plan at least annually (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Leads the CQI system, approves action plans, completes incident and mortality reviews and reports to the governing authority.
Maintains the data plan, runs surveys and summaries, convenes the team and tracks action items.
Submit complete monthly data, carry out assigned actions and share findings with staff.
Supplies health data and participates in incident and mortality reviews.
Reviews CQI reports and provides resources for improvement.

Monthly data submissions and tracking log
Quarterly CQI team minutes
Written satisfaction survey summary
Written outcomes assessment summary
Records of input from individuals, families and others
Action plans with owners, due dates and results
Internal incident review and mortality review records
Quarterly and annual CQI reports to the governing authority

policies.title: DDD/Medicaid Compliance, Fee-for-Service Billing and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: Executive director, billing and administrative staff, residence supervisors and direct support professionals
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] bills DDD and Medicaid only for services that were authorized, delivered and documented, pays the required wage pass-through correctly, and keeps records that support every claim.
policies.policy: Services are approved and paid through DDD as Individual Supports under the Community Care Program and Supports Program, which operate under the NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115), on a fee-for-service basis. [AGENCY NAME] bills only after a service has been delivered, only against a current DDD authorization, and only under an active Medicaid provider ID, since NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without one. Every claim is supported by daily and monthly documentation in the individual's record. [AGENCY NAME] does not falsify, alter or backdate records or claims. We pass through the required DSP and DSP Supervisor wage increase as base wage and never as a bonus or to cover operating costs. We keep records so that DDD, Medicaid and the Office of Licensing can verify the services billed.

definitions.definition: A payment method in which [AGENCY NAME] is paid for each authorized service delivered.
DDD's approval of a service, with the amount, frequency and dates for a specific individual.
The DDD service under which [AGENCY NAME] provides residential supports to individuals.
The identification number that identifies [AGENCY NAME] as an approved Medicaid provider and is required for claims.
A required increase in base wage for DSPs and DSP Supervisors funded by a DDD rate increase.
Knowingly making false entries in a record or claim, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.

procedures: The executive director confirms in writing, before the first claim, that [AGENCY NAME] is approved for Individual Supports and holds an active Medicaid provider ID. The administrative designee files the confirmation and re-checks the ID status every quarter.

The billing designee enters each DDD authorization into the billing system when received, recording the individual, service, units, rate, start date and end date. No claim is created for a service without an authorization on file.

Direct support professionals document the services delivered at the time of delivery, in the daily record (PCS-03). Where Electronic Visit Verification applies, they also clock in and out as set out in GOV-06.

By the 5th business day of each month, the residence supervisor reviews the prior month's daily records for completeness, signatures, dates and consistency with the plan. The supervisor gives corrections to staff within 2 business days. Corrections are made by dated, signed late entry, not by erasing or overwriting.

The responsible team member completes the monthly progress documentation required for each individual and files it in the record (REC-01). The residence supervisor verifies this before billing for that month is finalized.

The billing designee builds the claim from the verified records and compares units billed to units authorized and to units documented. No claim is submitted for services undocumented, outside the authorization period or above authorized units.
The executive director or a designee not involved in preparing the claim reviews the claim summary and approves it in writing before submission.
The billing designee submits claims within the DDD and Medicaid timelines, and keeps proof of the submission date.

Each month, the billing designee reconciles claims to authorizations and payments, and lists denied, adjusted and unpaid claims. The designee works each exception within 10 business days and records its cause and resolution.

For rate, code or authorization questions, the billing designee contacts the DDD Fee-for-Service Unit at the address published by DDD (currently DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov, to be confirmed against DDD's current communications) and keeps a copy of the question and the answer.

If an overpayment or billing error is found, the billing designee notifies the executive director within 2 business days. The agency stops billing the affected item, corrects or voids the claim as DDD or Medicaid instruct, and returns any overpayment promptly. The executive director records the cause and corrective action in the CQI log (GOV-04).

The executive director ensures that the DSP and DSP Supervisor wage increase from the 1/1/2026 rate change, about $0.46 per hour, was applied to base wage no later than 3/1/2026, with retroactive pay to 1/1/2026. The payroll designee documents the date, each affected employee, the hours covered and the amounts paid. It is not paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.
The payroll designee audits wage pass-through payments annually and whenever DDD issues a further rate change, and the executive director signs the audit.

If [AGENCY NAME]'s combined Community Care Program and Supports Program reimbursement reaches $350,000 or more, the executive director arranges an annual audit of the financial statements by an independent auditor and files the audit as DDD requires.

Staff who suspect billing or documentation errors, or are pressured to alter a record or claim, report to the executive director or [PHONE] without retaliation. The executive director investigates, and documented falsification leads to disciplinary action and is reported as required (STF-06).

The administrative designee retains billing, authorization and supporting service records in line with REC-01, and gives them to DDD, Medicaid, the Office of Licensing and other authorized reviewers on request.
The executive director reviews this policy annually, and whenever DDD changes rates, rules or billing guidance (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures billing integrity, approves claims, ensures wage pass-through and answers to DDD and Medicaid.
Enters authorizations, prepares and submits claims, reconciles and works denials.
Applies and documents the wage pass-through.
Verifies daily and monthly documentation before billing and corrects deficiencies.
Document services accurately and on time, and never alter records.

DDD authorizations log
Daily and monthly service documentation
Claim summaries with approval signatures and submission proof
Monthly reconciliation and exception log
Overpayment and correction records
Wage pass-through payroll records and annual audit
Annual financial statement audit, if required
Correspondence with DDD Fee-for-Service Unit

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)
policies.applies_to: Direct support professionals, residence supervisors, executive director and billing staff
policies.purpose: To make sure services subject to Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) under the 21st Century Cures Act and the DDD program are recorded electronically at the point of service and reconciled before billing.
policies.policy: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care and home health services. New Jersey applies it to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through the HHAeXchange system. [AGENCY NAME] records every EVV-covered visit electronically at the point of service, resolves exceptions promptly and accurately, and reconciles EVV data to the daily record and the authorization before any claim is submitted. A Live-In Worker Attestation is used only where the worker actually lives with the person served. EVV records are never entered to show service that did not occur, and no staff may clock in or out for another person.

definitions.definition: An electronic system that records the type of service, individual served, date, location, worker, and start and end times of a visit.
The vendor system New Jersey uses for DDD EVV.
A visit record with missing, mismatched or manually edited data that needs review and correction before billing.
A signed attestation that allows exclusion from EVV where the worker lives with the person served.
The place where the service is actually delivered.

procedures: The executive director determines which [AGENCY NAME] services and staff are covered by EVV, and records the determination by service, residence and shift. The determination is reviewed whenever DDD issues updated EVV guidance, and current compliance deadlines are confirmed with DDD.
The executive director names an EVV administrator who maintains staff and individual profiles in HHAeXchange, controls access and serves as the contact for DDD and the vendor.
The EVV administrator sets up each individual and each worker in the system before the worker's first covered shift, and removes access on the day a worker separates from employment.
Each DSP receives EVV training at orientation (STF-03) and again whenever the process changes. The trainer documents the training, and the DSP signs acknowledgment.

At the start of each covered visit, the DSP clocks in at the point of service by the method assigned. At the end of the visit, the DSP clocks out. The DSP never clocks in or out for another employee and never records a visit before it begins or after it ends.

If the system cannot be used (for example, loss of connectivity, device failure), the DSP notifies the residence supervisor or on-call manager at once (STF-08), records the actual start and end times on paper, and enters or submits the visit through the approved exception process as soon as the system is available.

The residence supervisor checks the EVV exception report at least weekly. Exceptions (missed clock-ins, overlapping or mismatched times, edits) are reviewed within 3 business days. The supervisor interviews the DSP, confirms the facts, makes the correction through the approved process with a reason code, and documents it.

A manual edit is made only to correct a verified error, with a documented reason, the editor's name and date. If a visit did not occur, it is not added. The EVV administrator reports repeated or suspicious edits to the executive director.

Where a worker lives in the home with the person served, the executive director may use the Live-In Worker Attestation only after confirming that the worker's primary residence is with the person. The attestation is signed, filed and reviewed at least annually and whenever the living arrangement changes. If the worker no longer lives there, EVV is applied from the date of the change.

Before billing each month, the billing designee reconciles EVV visit data to the daily service records and to the DDD authorization (GOV-05). Services are billed only for visits that are verified in EVV or properly excluded. Unresolved discrepancies are held until corrected.

The EVV administrator reviews every month's data to measure the share of visits that were verified without manual edit and the number of exceptions by residence and worker, and gives the results to the CQI team (GOV-04).
The executive director addresses EVV non-compliance by retraining, counseling or discipline, and treats any falsified EVV entry as falsification of records (STF-06).

For helpdesk or policy questions, the EVV administrator uses the contact on the DDD EVV page and the HHAeXchange support channel, [DDD EVV HELPDESK CONTACT], and keeps a record of questions and answers.
EVV records are retained according to REC-01 and are available to DDD, Medicaid and the Office of Licensing on request.
The executive director reviews this policy at least annually and whenever DDD changes EVV requirements (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Determines EVV coverage, designates the EVV administrator, approves live-in attestations and addresses non-compliance.
Maintains profiles and access, trains staff, monitors exceptions and acts as contact for DDD and the vendor.
Reviews and resolves exceptions weekly and ensures staff clock in and out correctly.
Clock in and out accurately at the point of service and report system problems immediately.
Reconciles EVV data to records and authorizations before claims are submitted.

documentation: EVV coverage determination by service and residence
EVV training records and acknowledgments
Weekly exception reports and resolution notes
Manual edit log with reasons
Live-In Worker Attestations and annual reviews

policies.title: Licensing Inspections, Deficiencies, Plans of Correction and Enforcement Readiness
policies.applies_to: Licensee/Executive Director, Residence Supervisors, in-charge staff and all employees at every community residence and supervised apartment operated by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep [AGENCY NAME] ready for licensing inspections at all times, so that every inspection, announced or not, proceeds smoothly. To make sure each cited deficiency is corrected promptly and in writing, and that the agency tracks changes in State enforcement authority.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only with the authorization of the NJ DHS Office of Licensing. Each residence is open to inspection or investigation by DHS without limitation or notice. This covers records, equipment, sanitary conditions, accommodations and the management of individuals (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4). An annual on-site inspection is required, and unannounced inspections are increasing beginning in 2026. Staff cooperate fully and courteously with every inspector and never obstruct, delay or conceal records. Each residence is kept inspection-ready every day. Any deficiency (noncompliance with a rule in N.J.A.C. 10:44A) is answered in writing by the deadline in the notice, is corrected, and is verified through the CQI system. The Executive Director follows the enhanced DHS enforcement authority created by P.L.2025, c.280 (effective January 2026), and legal counsel reviews its penalty provisions.

definitions.definition: Noncompliance with a rule in N.J.A.C. 10:44A, as cited by the Office of Licensing.
The agency's written response to cited deficiencies. It states the corrective action, the person responsible, the completion date and how the agency will keep the correction in place.
A license that may be issued when an inspection finds only partial compliance. Two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal.
Written permission from the Office of Licensing to keep operating past license expiration when an inspection is delayed (see N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3).
The staff person assigned at each residence to receive inspectors, provide records and escort them.

procedures: The Executive Director confirms that each residence has a current license or written authorization to operate before individuals are served, and posts or keeps the license where inspectors can see it. No residence operates without Office of Licensing authorization.

The Executive Director assigns an inspection host and a backup host for each residence, and lists them in the residence's emergency/administrative contact sheet. The host is the person in charge on that shift if no one else has been named.

Inspections may occur at any hour without notice. On arrival, the host asks for identification, welcomes the inspector, and calls the Residence Supervisor and the Executive Director at [PHONE] immediately. The inspection is never delayed while waiting for management to arrive.

The host gives inspectors access to all areas of the residence, including bedrooms (with the individual's agreement and privacy respected), kitchens, medication storage, the physical plant and vehicles, together with records, equipment and individuals who wish to speak with them. Staff do not coach individuals on what to say, and no one retaliates against anyone who speaks with an inspector.
The host keeps a log of the inspector's name, agency, arrival and departure times, areas inspected, records requested and records copied.

Each residence keeps a standing Inspection Readiness Binder, or a secured electronic equivalent, that is reviewed monthly. It holds the current license, staff files, the two-week schedules, credentials and training records, background check and Central Registry/Child Abuse Registry documentation, physical plant records (fire drills, inspections, maintenance), and insurance documents.
Individual files stay at the residence (see REC-01) and are available on request. Staff files are available at the residence or within a time the Executive Director agrees with the inspector.

The Residence Supervisor completes an internal mock inspection of the residence at least quarterly, using the licensing checklist. Findings go to the Executive Director and are tracked in the CQI plan (GOV-04).
Once the inspector gives an exit summary or issues a written report, the Executive Director reviews every cited deficiency within one business day and identifies the deadline stated in the notice.

The Executive Director responds in writing by the notice deadline. The written response includes a POC for each deficiency stating the corrective action, the responsible person, the completion date and how the correction will be monitored. If more time is needed, the Executive Director asks the Office of Licensing in writing before the deadline.

Immediate health and safety hazards are corrected at once, and no later than the same day, and the correction is documented. Where individuals are at risk, the Executive Director takes interim protective measures and documents them.

The Residence Supervisor confirms completion of each corrective action, attaches proof (receipts, training sign-in sheets, photographs, revised records) to the POC file, and reports completion to the Executive Director.
The Executive Director verifies the correction by follow-up review 30 and 90 days after completion and records the results. Any repeat finding is escalated to the governing authority.
The Executive Director reports deficiency trends and the status of every open POC to the governing authority at least quarterly.

If a provisional license is issued, the Executive Director convenes a corrective action meeting within five business days, assigns an owner to each outstanding item, and reports progress to the governing authority at least monthly until a full license is issued.

Each January and at each annual manual review (GOV-03), the Executive Director consults legal counsel about P.L.2025, c.280 and any related DHS notices, and updates this policy and training if enforcement authority or penalties change.
The Executive Director trains all in-charge staff on this policy during orientation and annually, including how to host an unannounced inspection.

responsibilities.duty: Receive quarterly reports on inspections and POCs, require corrective action, and ensure legal review of enforcement authority.
Maintain licensure, respond in writing to citations by the deadline, supervise POCs and verify their effectiveness.
Keep the residence inspection-ready, run quarterly mock inspections, and carry out and document corrective actions.
Receive inspectors, give full access to records and areas, notify management immediately and keep the inspection log.
Review P.L.2025, c.280 penalty provisions and advise on enforcement actions.

documentation: Current license and any written authorization to operate
Inspection log for each visit
Inspector reports, notices of deficiency and exit summaries
Written POCs, submission proof and proof of correction
Monthly readiness binder review and quarterly mock inspection reports
30- and 90-day verification records
Governing authority quarterly reports
Training sign-in sheets

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors and volunteers, and all individuals served at every residence and supervised apartment of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual enjoys the same rights as other citizens, is supported to understand and use those rights, and lives in a home that meets home and community-based settings requirements.
policies.policy: Individuals served by [AGENCY NAME] have the same rights as all other citizens, and exercising a right is never prohibited or used as grounds for retribution (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-3.1). The agency complies with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. Staff know and observe the rights in the Division's rights document, and each individual receives that document and signs an acknowledgment on admission. Individuals are trained and supported to understand their options, make choices and exercise their rights. Rights are never limited because an individual has a guardian or family. Because DDD services are authorized under the NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115) and New Jersey's HCBS Statewide Transition Plan applies to 10:44A homes, each residence also ensures privacy, choice, community access and control over daily life as described in this policy.

definitions.definition: The Division's document listing the rights of individuals with developmental disabilities, given to each individual and guardian on admission.

The federal standards at 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) and the New Jersey HCBS Statewide Transition Plan, which require that the home be integrated in the community, chosen by the individual, and respectful of privacy, dignity, autonomy and independence.
A person legally appointed to make decisions for an individual. The guardian's appointment does not remove the individual's own rights.
Any punishment, threat, loss of privilege, change in staffing or other adverse treatment in response to an individual exercising a right.

procedures: At or before admission, the Residence Supervisor gives the individual and the guardian (if any) the Division's rights document in the individual's preferred language and format, and reviews it aloud or in an accessible way.

The individual, and the guardian if there is one, signs an acknowledgment of receipt. The Residence Supervisor files it in the individual's record within two business days. If the individual declines to sign, staff document the date, how the rights were explained and the reason given.

The Executive Director trains every new employee on the rights document and this policy during orientation, before the employee works alone, and again annually. Training sign-in sheets go in the personnel file.

Within 30 days of admission and at least annually after that, the individual's team discusses rights in a manner suited to the individual (plain language, pictures, role-play), and documents what the individual understands and what further support is needed.

Staff support each individual to practice choosing: when to wake and sleep, what to eat, how to spend free time, who visits, what to wear and how to decorate his or her bedroom. Staff offer real choices and document teaching and support in the daily notes.

Each individual has privacy in the bedroom and bathroom. Staff knock and wait for permission before entering. Bedrooms may be locked with a key held by the individual unless a restriction has been approved under IR-02.

Individuals may have visitors at the times they choose, subject only to house rules developed with the individuals and applied under IR-02. Individuals may use the telephone, mail and electronic communication privately.
Individuals have access to food and drink at any time, including the kitchen and pantry, consistent with any modified diet ordered under HES-04. Any limit needs an approved restriction under IR-02.

Staff support individuals to access the community, including shopping, religion, recreation, voting and work or volunteering, as described in PCS-05, and to control their own schedules and money, as described in IR-06.

Staff never limit, deny or discourage a right because the individual has a guardian or family member who disagrees. Staff tell the Residence Supervisor, who consults the Executive Director and, if needed, the Human Rights Committee (IR-03).

Staff report to the Residence Supervisor, within the same shift, any observation that an individual's rights were violated. The Residence Supervisor notifies the Executive Director within one business day. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately under BSP-03.

If an individual says he or she is being punished, threatened or treated differently for using a right, the Executive Director investigates within three business days, protects the individual from further retaliation and documents the result. Staff who retaliate are subject to discipline up to termination.
The Executive Director supports each individual's self-advocacy, including connecting individuals to self-advocacy groups, advocacy organizations, and the grievance process in IR-04.

At least annually, the Executive Director and Residence Supervisor review each residence against the HCBS settings elements in this policy, and verify that current N.J.A.C. 10:44A and DDD standards are reflected. They record findings and corrective actions in the CQI plan (GOV-04).
The Executive Director reports rights complaints, restriction requests and HCBS review results to the governing authority at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure rights training, annual HCBS settings review and corrective action; investigate retaliation.
Provide the rights document and obtain acknowledgments, support choice-making, and report suspected violations.
Observe and support each individual's rights, respect privacy and choices, and report violations.
Are encouraged to use their rights, ask questions and tell the agency of any concern.
Review any proposed limit on rights under IR-02 and IR-03.

documentation: Signed rights acknowledgment for each individual (and guardian)
Staff training sign-in sheets and rights training content
Team rights discussion notes
Daily/monthly notes showing choice support
Records of retaliation or rights-violation reports and investigations
Annual HCBS settings review and corrective actions
Quarterly report to governing authority

policies.title: Rights Restrictions, House Rules and Due Process
policies.applies_to: Executive Director, Residence Supervisors, planning teams, direct support staff and the Human Rights Committee for all residences of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure house rules are fair and developed with the individuals who live in the home, and that any limit on an individual's rights is rare, justified, reviewed and time-limited.
policies.policy: House rules at [AGENCY NAME] are developed with the individuals affected, are necessary to promote order, and do not infringe on the rights of others or endanger others (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-3.1). No house rule or staff practice may override an individual's rights. An individual-specific restriction is used only when there is a documented assessed need, after less restrictive alternatives have been tried, with informed consent, a time limit and regular review. Each restriction is reviewed by the Human Rights Committee in accordance with N.J.A.C. 10:41A before it is put into effect, except in an emergency that is handled under BSP-02. Restraint, seclusion and other restrictive interventions follow BSP-02 and the health and safety requirements of N.J.A.C. 10:44A Subchapter 5 (10:44A-5.1 to 5.8).

definitions.definition: A written expectation that applies to everyone in the residence and exists for order and safety, developed with the individuals who live there.
Any individual-specific limit on a right or HCBS setting element, including privacy, access to food, visitors, locked doors, money and movement.
A positive support, environmental change or teaching strategy that addresses the same risk without limiting a right.
The individual's opportunity to be told of a proposed restriction, to disagree, to be heard with a representative or advocate, and to have the decision reviewed.

procedures: The Residence Supervisor holds a house meeting with the individuals at least every quarter, and whenever a new rule is proposed, to discuss existing and proposed house rules. Rules are written in plain, accessible language.

Each proposed house rule is tested against three questions: Is it necessary to promote order? Does it infringe on anyone's rights? Does it endanger anyone? A rule that fails any of the three is not adopted. The outcome and the individuals' comments are recorded in the minutes.
